new_entities.name: Sugar-sweetened beverage taxes
new_entities.description: Population-level fiscal policies that increase the price of sugar-sweetened beverages through taxation.

new_entities.name: Population beverage consumption
aliases: beverage consumption at the population level
new_entities.description: Population-level purchasing or consumption of taxed beverages and close substitutes.

edges.effect_quant: A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis of 62 quantitative studies found that implemented SSB taxes were associated with a 15% reduction in taxed beverage sales and a price elasticity of demand of -1.59, while a 2019 review found that the equivalent of a 10% SSB tax cut purchases and consumption by about 10% on average.
edges.population: general populations living in jurisdictions that implemented sugar-sweetened beverage excise taxes
edges.mechanism: Taxes raise retail prices, reduce demand for taxed beverages, and can also encourage reformulation or substitution toward untaxed drinks such as water.
edges.summary: Sugar-sweetened beverage taxes reliably reduce population purchases and sales of taxed drinks overall. The effect is one of the clearest population-level nutrition policy signals in the literature.
edges.caveats: Magnitude varies by tax size, structure, enforcement, local market conditions, and whether analyses focus on sales, purchases, or self-reported intake. Substitution patterns and cross-border shopping can attenuate or redistribute effects in some settings.
